content: {"summary":"Writes were refused because Redis' background‑save (BGSAVE) fork failed with “Cannot allocate memory”, triggered by the OS strict overcommit setting (vm.overcommit_memory=2) which capped total commitments at ~25.6 GB; the 14 GB dataset plus the forked copy exceeded this limit, causing MISCONF.","likely_cause":"OS strict memory overcommit (vm.overcommit_memory=2) caused the BGSAVE fork to exceed the commit limit, leading to MISCONF and write refusals.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"The host was configured with vm.overcommit_memory=2 (ratio 80), limiting total memory commitments to about 25.6 GB.","evidence_ids":["RB-019#4"],"quote":"vm.overcommit_memory=2 (ratio 80) on this VM."},{"text":"During BGSAVE Redis forks a child that needs roughly double its current 14 GB usage (~28 GB), exceeding the 25.6 GB commit limit and causing fork failure.","evidence_ids":["INC-0078#1"],"quote":"so 14 GB plus 14 GB asks for roughly 28 GB, more than 25.6 GB."},{"text":"Resetting vm.overcommit_memory to 1 allowed the snapshot to complete and writes to be accepted again.","evidence_ids":["RB-019#3"],"quote":"ssh redis-features-01.prod.internal 'sudo sysctl -w vm.overcommit_memory=1'"}],"next_checks":["Check vm.overcommit_memory setting on all Redis nodes","Verify commit limit vs Redis used memory on each host","Monitor BGSAVE success after restoring overcommit setting","Audit platform hardening baseline to prevent unintended strict overcommit changes"]}
